prompt: The client wants to cut the number of customers it loses each year. Which takeaway matters most?

exhibit.title: Customers and renewal rate by tenure

options.text: Customers of three years or more are the largest group
options.feedback: True, but they renew at 88%, so they lose fewer customers than the first-year group.

options.text: The longest-tenure group loses the most, since it is four times larger
First-year customers account for the most losses, about 5,500 a year
options.feedback: Right. Lost each year: first year 10,000 × 55% = 5,500; second year 20,000 × 20% = 4,000; third year or more 40,000 × 12% = 4,800.
The table shows renewal rates, not why customers leave.

explanation: Customers lost each year = customers × (1 − renewal rate): first year 5,500, second year 4,000, third year or more 4,800.

extras.proof: Customers lost each year = customers × (1 − renewal rate): first year 5,500, second year 4,000, third year or more 4,800.
